blocks.text: XPath Cheatsheet for Test Automation Engineers
Bookmark this. Seriously. When you have 2 hours before a release and need to find that one stubborn element that broke your test, you'll be back here.

This is the cheatsheet version of XPath for Test Automation: From \"I Hate This\" to \"I Write It in My Sleep\". No stories, no philosophy , just copy-paste patterns that work. Every expression here was born from "why doesn't this #$ percent element select?" moments at 11pm.

Story: I once wrote a beautiful XPath based on CSS class selectors. Worked for 6 months. Then CSS classes changed in a refactor, and 80 tests exploded the same day. I learned: priority matters.
Reach for the top first. Descend only when you must. This pyramid exists so your selectors survive refactors.

War story: I debugged for 3 hours why my XPath to select case-insensitive elements wasn't working. I'd written: //a[lower-case(@href)='/help']. Looked right. Returned nothing. Silent failure , no error message, just empty results. Turns out, lower-case() is XPath 2.0, and browsers only support 1.0. I had to switch to translate() instead. Now I know: if you see 2.0 features in the docs, they're silently broken in the browser. Use only XPath 1.0 or go server-side. WebDriver, Playwright, and Cypress all evaluate 1.0 for By.xpath/xpath=. /cy.xpath().
Many "filter by content" patterns need XPath 2.0+ (Playwright's getByText, Cypress's .contains() are usually easier). Stick to XPath 1.0 expressions above unless you've explicitly opted in.
Same XPath. Five flavors of API.
NoSuchElementException ≠ "element missing forever." Could be iframe context wrong. Wrap with driver.switchTo().frame(...) or .defaultContent().
findElement vs findElements. Singular throws on empty; plural returns list. Use plural when 0/1/many is acceptable.
Implicit waits stack across tests. Always reset in @BeforeEach or your setup hook.
Stale element refs happen after DOM mutation. Re-find; don't cache element references across page transitions.
XPath 1.0 only. for $i in . , regex, lower-case with Unicode normalization , all 2.0+ and silently fail.
Strict mode is on by default , locator() returning >1 match throws. Use .first() / .nth(i) deliberately.
Locators are lazy. They re-resolve on every action. That's a feature, not a bug. Don't call .elementHandle() unless you need the snapshot.
Auto-retries are unlimited by default within expect(). Use expect(locator).toBeVisible() rather than .waitFor() + .isVisible().
XPath auto-pierces shadow DOM via >>> chains. Pure XPath alone does not , use page.locator('css=host-element >>> inner-shadow-html').
Prefer semantic over xpath when the role is unambiguous: getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }) beats //button[normalize-space()='Pay'].
XPath needs the plugin (cypress-xpath). Out of the box, Cypress is CSS-first.
.contains() is the Cypress-native way to do "contains text" , easier than XPath substring for visible-text filters.
Auto-retry is built in. cy.get(locator).should('be.visible') polls for you.
Element isolation: tests run inside one giant iframe; explicit shadow-DOM traversal rarely needed but XPath-on-shadow still won't pierce.
cy.xpath() returns a wrapper, not a DOM element. Chain .click() / .type() directly.
Some signals that you should reach for a different tool:
You're matching visible text only. Use Playwright's getByText('Sign in') or Cypress's cy.contains('Sign in') , both auto-retry.
You need a screenshot/visual assertion. XPath finds nodes, not pixels. Reach for image-diff tools (Playwright's expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()).
You're chaining into shadow DOM. Use Playwright's >>> selector syntax , it's purpose-built.
You need cross-origin iframe traversal. XPath stops at iframe boundaries regardless of tool. Switch contexts, or use CDP/BiDi for snapshot diff.
You're navigating the accessibility tree. That's ARIA's job , use semantic locators instead.
The locator depends on element coordinates. XPath can't. Use Relative Locator (Selenium 4: above/below/near) or locator.boundingBox() (Playwright).
This section is for SDETs shipping production test suites in Selenium, Playwright, or Cypress. The XPaths above are correct; this section makes them survive.
10.1 Where XPath lives in your POM
The locator is a property, not a method. Locators as By/Locator constants on the page object , never inline strings in test specs.
